# Information ratio (`information_ratio`)

*Category: Benchmark-relative analysis · Nature: estimated · Unit: ratio · Formula id: `information_ratio@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Active return per unit of tracking error, annualized.

## 2. Formula

```text
P * mean(a_t) / (std(a_t, ddof=1) * sqrt(P)), a_t = r_fund,t - r_bench,t
```

## 3. Required inputs

Fund and benchmark returns on aligned periods with a regular frequency. A benchmark is required.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

How consistently the fund beat (or lagged) its benchmark relative to how much it deviated from it.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Arithmetic ex-post Information Ratio (Grinold & Kahn), equal to the Sharpe ratio of active returns. PerformanceAnalytics divides the difference of geometric annualized returns instead.

## 7. Assumptions

- Square-root-of-time scaling.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- The benchmark is not representative of the strategy's opportunity set.
- The overlap with the benchmark is short.
- Returns are smoothed.
- Tracking error is tiny.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap. (policy `benchmark_simple`: Requires at least 2 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 (R) | `InformationRatio` | no (documented difference) | Uses ActivePremium (geometric) / TrackingError. |
| QuantStats 0.0.81 | `stats.information_ratio` | no (documented difference) | QuantStats reports the non-annualized per-period ratio. |

## 11. Sources

- Grinold, R. C., & Kahn, R. N. (2000). Active Portfolio Management (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.
- Goodwin, T. H. (1998). The Information Ratio. Financial Analysts Journal, 54(4), 34-43.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Arithmetic active mean over tracking error (decision 0012).
